title: Mandatory climate-related financial reporting
summary: Large companies and other entities must report climate-related risks and opportunities in a sustainability report, phased in from financial years starting 1 January 2025, under amendments to the Corporations Act.

instruments.title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Financial Market Infrastructure and Other Measures) Act 2024
instruments.provisions: Schedule 4: sustainability reporting in the Corporations Act 2001

commenced.what: Reporting obligations begin for the first group of entities

direction_rationale: The reports add preparation and assurance costs for large entities; better information on climate risk may help investors price it.

verified.notes: Assent from the Federal Register; Schedule 4 commenced on 18 September 2024. The 1 January 2025 start of phased reporting is from the Productivity Commission (2025, citing ASIC) and the Act's transitional provisions.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 29 October 2026 (tranche 3: laws in regulatory regimes with no register items) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: Mandatory sustainability reports add preparation and assurance costs for large entities, phased in by size. The benefit of better information on climate risk for investors is real but not measured.

marks.reason: New reports, and later assurance, for large entities across the economy.

assessment.confidence_note: No estimate of compliance costs or benefits was found in the sources used.
